title: A patchy dust screen fails a three-color CPV test for opacity index at most two under nominal wavelength and independent error assumptions
abstract: We test whether free dust columns can repair optical color residuals in a complex periodic variable. Every foreground screen with shared stellar color weights has a depth that is concave in opacity. This gives a linear three-color test without a column model. For 11 ground-based depths of TIC 262400835 on three nights, the strongest violation at opacity index 2 is 4.136 standard errors. A correction for 24 pair and triple tests gives a probability bound of 0.000425 under nominal wavelengths and independent Gaussian errors. Concavity also excludes smaller positive indices under these assumptions. This is not a dust composition measurement. An added independent error of 0.103 percentage points reaches the corrected 5% boundary. Unknown cross-band covariance can remove the rejection, and full bandpass integration was not done. Code, proof, aggregate diagnostics and source hashes are supplied. The result identifies a measurement and model check before the colors are used to infer grain physics.

display.caption: The column-mixture test, its sensitivity to added error, and a synthetic screen that obeys the bound. Wavelength and error assumptions are stated in the text.
